english_abstract: This paper investigates grant-free random access in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. We firstly propose a multi-frame transmission scheme with affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) to handle the large differential delay and Doppler shift at the satellite receiver, and derive the input-output relationship. Subsequently, we learn a score-based generative channel prior directly on the AFDM effective channel with fractional delay and Doppler, without restrictive sparse or grid-aligned channel assumptions. The training uses colored Gaussian noise to account for correlations in the denoiser input error. The learned prior is then incorporated into a message passing (MP) receiver for joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE). Within this receiver, a learned density ratio estimator uses the input and output of the minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) channel denoiser for activity detection. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed receiver outperforms the baseline receiver in terms of activity detection and channel estimation.
